paragraphs: Qodem sheyyatchil bitpillat haamida kesheomer "gaal yisrael" yemashmesh bitpillin shel rosh, ki tepillin shel rosh hu baatzilut, utepillat haamida baatzilut, veyesh omerim sheggam besiyyum "hambarek et ammo yisrael bashshalom" yemashmesh bitpillin shel rosh, veayyen bekap hachayyim siman tv ot b', venireh li dehannoheg kak lo yemashmesh ella achar "yihyu leratzon imre pi", ki pasuq zeh kullo mikkelal hattepilla, vetzarik laamod yadayv keputim zeh al zeh keabda qamme mearyeh, velaken lo yarim et yado ad sheyyesayyem pasuq zeh:

clarification.explanation: Before beginning the Amidah, when saying "Ga'al Yisrael" at the conclusion of the blessings of the Shema, one should touch the head tefillin, because according to the kabbalistic tradition both the head tefillin and the Amidah belong to the world of Atzilut. Some say that at the conclusion of the Amidah as well, at "Who blesses His people Israel with peace," one should touch the head tefillin. It seems to the Ben Ish Chai that one who follows this practice should touch them only after finishing "Yihyu leratzon imrei fi," because this verse is part of the prayer, and one must stand in prayer with his hands folded one over the other like a servant before his master; therefore he should not raise his hand to touch them until he finishes this verse.
takeaways: Touches the head tefillin when saying "Ga'al Yisrael" before the Amidah
Some also follow the practice of touching them at the conclusion of the Amidah
One who touches them at the conclusion should do so only after "Yihyu leratzon"
In prayer one stands like a servant before his master, hands folded one over the other

paragraphs: Kesheomed lehitpallel yekavven raglayv lihyot shavim udebuqim zeh im zeh beyosher kede lehiddamot lemalakim diktib behu "veraglehem regel yeshara" (yechezqel , z), veod yesh teamim acherim bazeh, uminhag hasseparaddim kesheomedim lehitpallel tepillat haamida qodem hattepilla mehappekim penehem qetzat laachorehem veosim tenua bidehem laanashim haomedim baachorehem o betziddehem, vehattaam bazeh gam ken lehiddamot lemalakim sheddarkam lihyot meqabbelim ol malkut shamayim zeh mizzeh, venotenim reshut zeh lazeh, lehorot al achdut veachava shebbenehem kelomar kullanu keechad anachnu maskimim bemachshaba achat ubedaat achat leqabbel ol malkut shamayim ubazeh yitalleh veyitromem qilluso shel hqb"h keshehu naaseh mittok haachdut vehaahaba, uledugmat zeh hu minhag hasseparaddim hannizkar, vehaggaon mehara"n shappira asa taam leminhag zeh al pi hassod uqelisiyya, ulepi hattaam shello apillu im en adam acher betziddo o acharayv gam ken yaaseh ken:

clarification.explanation: When standing to pray, one should position his feet evenly and joined together in a straight line, in order to resemble the angels, of whom it is said "and their feet were a straight foot." There are additional reasons for this as well. The custom of the Sephardim is that before the Amidah they turn their faces slightly backward and make a gesture with their hands to the people standing behind them or beside them. This reason too is to resemble the angels, whose way is to accept the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven from one another and to grant permission to one another, so as to indicate the unity and fellowship among them — that is, that we all agree with a single mind to accept the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, and through unity and love the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated. And according to the reason given based on the Kabbalah, even if there is no other person beside him or behind him, he should still do so.
takeaways: Positions his feet evenly and joined together in a straight line, to resemble the angels
The Sephardic custom is to turn slightly backward and make a gesture to those standing around him
The reason is to arouse unity in accepting the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven
According to the kabbalistic reason, one should do so even when no one is standing around him

paragraphs: Im omed lehitpallel bemaqom shehu yosheb bo, yizzaher lachazor laachorayv shiur shelosh pesiot, veyachazor laamod bimqomo lehitpallel, veim hu yosheb rachoq mimmaqom sheomed bo lehitpallel yelek techilla lemaqom sheomed lehitpallel bo, veyachazor laachorayv shelosh pesiot, veyachazor leoto maqom sheomed bo battepilla, deyesh sod bazeh lachazor laachorayv shelosh pesiot qodem sheyyatchil lehitpallel, veal pi happeshat hem zeker leotam shelosh milin shechazeru yisrael laachorehem bemaamad har sinay vechazeru venitqarebu:

clarification.explanation: If one is praying in a place where he is already sitting, he should be careful to step back a distance of three steps, and then return to stand in his place to pray. And if he is sitting far from the place where he will stand to pray, he should first go to the place of prayer, and from there step back three steps, and then return to that same place to stand in prayer. There is a secret in stepping back three steps before prayer, and according to the plain meaning they are in remembrance of the three mil that Israel retreated backward at the standing at Mount Sinai, and afterward returned and drew near again.
takeaways: Before prayer, one steps back three steps and then returns to his place
If sitting far away, he first goes to the place of prayer and then steps back from there
In remembrance of the three mil that Israel retreated at Mount Sinai and then drew near again

paragraphs: Hammitpallel tzarik sheyyekavven belibbo perush hammillot shemmotzi mippiv veyachshob shekina kenegdo, veyasir veyidcheh kol machashabot hattoredot oto ad shettishshaer kavvanato umachashabto zaka bitpillato, dehattepilla hi bimqom haqqarebban umachshaba zara poselet beqadashim, veim roeh atzmo mekavven yapeh bitpillato al yachshob sheabur zeh rauy shettaaseh baqqashato, ki zeh niqra iyyun tepilla venizkarin aonotayv, ella yachshebu ulay yishma hashshem yitbarak beqareu elayv baabur otzem rachamayv vegadol chasadayv sheshshomea tepillat kol peh bemiddat hachesed veharachamim, ulepi dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l tzarik sheyyekavven kak, yadanu Adonai sheen anachnu reuyim vahagunim lehitpallel lepaneka, abal samaknu al rachameka harabbim vachasadeka haggedolim ki chapetz chesed umarbeh lehetib atta, vekakkatub "tob Adonai lakkol verachamayv al kol maasayv" (tehillim qmh, t), veatta tzivvitanu lehitpallel eleka ki atta elohenu vaanachnu abadeka veenenu leka teluyot keene abadim el yad adonehem ad kan debarayv, vetzarik kol adam lehizzaher lekavven bekak:

clarification.explanation: One who prays must concentrate in his heart on the meaning of the words he utters, and think of the Divine Presence as facing him, and must push away every distracting thought until his intent remains pure, since prayer stands in place of the sacrifice and an alien thought disqualifies sacred offerings. And if he sees that he is concentrating well, he should not think that on account of this his request deserves to be granted, for this is called "scrutinizing one's prayer" and it arouses the remembrance of his sins; rather he should think that perhaps the Lord will hear his prayer out of the abundance of His mercy and kindness, for He hears the prayer of every mouth. And according to the Ari, one should have in mind: "We know, O Lord, that we are not worthy or fitting to pray before You, but we have relied upon Your abundant mercy and Your great kindness, for You desire kindness and abound in doing good, and You have commanded us to pray to You, for You are our God and we are Your servants, and our eyes are directed to You."
takeaways: One who prays concentrates on the meaning of the words and thinks of the Divine Presence facing him
He pushes away alien thoughts, since prayer stands in place of the sacrifice and an alien thought disqualifies sacred offerings
He should not rely on his own good concentration as a merit, for that is called "scrutinizing prayer," which arouses the remembrance of one's sins
He should have in mind that we rely on God's mercy and kindness, and not on our own merit

paragraphs: Hammitpallel tzarik lekavven bekol habberakot, veim achar amal vetorach vehishtaddelut rab eno yakol lekavven bekullam, yishtaddel veyitammetz lepachot lekavven b"abot" shehi beraka rishona veap al gab demin haddin im lo kivven b"abot" eno yotze yede choba vetzarik lachazor, katebu haacharonim debazzeman hazzeh en chozerin mishshum chesron kavvana, deshemma gam bachazarato lo yekavven. vehaggaon morenu harab chayyim mvlvz'n za"l natan etza lekol adam sheyyetzayyer bedato tzurat haotiyyot shemmotzi mippiv, veal yede kak mukrach shettihyeh kavvanato shelema. vetamo venimmuqo immo dibre pi chakam chen, mihu haoseh ken i epshar lo lehitpallel im hatztzibbur demukrach sheyyaarik harbeh bitpillato, ak bibraka rishona bilbad epshar laasot ken, velaken kol adam yizzaher lehargil atzmo bekak bishlosha rishonot o lepachot bibraka rishona:

clarification.explanation: One who prays must have intent in all the blessings, and if after great toil he is unable to concentrate in all of them, he should strive at least to concentrate in the first blessing, "Avot." And even though strictly by law, one who did not have intent in "Avot" has not fulfilled his obligation and must repeat the prayer, the later authorities wrote that nowadays one does not repeat the prayer for lack of intent, lest even upon repeating it he fail to concentrate again. And Rabbi Chaim of Volozhin gave the advice that a person picture in his mind the shape of the letters he utters, and thereby his intent will be complete. But one who does so cannot pray with the congregation, since he is forced to prolong his prayer considerably, so it is possible to do this only in the first blessing. Every person should accustom himself to this in the first three blessings, or at least in the first blessing.
takeaways: Concentrates in all the blessings, and at the very least in the blessing of "Avot"
Nowadays one does not repeat the prayer for lack of intent, lest he fail to concentrate even upon repeating it
The advice of Rabbi Chaim of Volozhin: to picture in one's mind the shape of the letters
One should accustom himself to this in the first three blessings, or at least in the first blessing

paragraphs: Tzarik laasot shette keriot ushette zeqipot bishat shemmishtachaveh baamida, ketzad kesheomer "baruk" yikra betebat "baruk" keriat haggup bilbad, ubetebat "atta" yikra et rosho gam ken, hare shette keriot, ukesheomer "Adonai" yizqop sham shette zeqipot, utechilla yizqop gupo bilbad, veachar kak yizqop rosho gam ken, remez laddabar "kaasher yachanu ken yissau" (bammidbar b, yz) velaken amar rab baggemara kol hakkorea korea bebaruk vekol hazzoqep zoqep beshem, denaqet bilshono hattahor lashon kapul bikriot vegam bizqipot, dela amar yikra bebaruk vezoqep beshem, vekannizkar kol zeh bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot(), vehakkeria tihyeh ad sheyyitpaqqequ kol chulyot shebbashshidra, dehaynu sheyyihyu boletin kol haqqesharim shebbepirqe chulyotayv, veim hu zaqen o choleh sheeno yakol lishchot kol kak, kevan shehirkin rosho dayyo vekannizkar baacharonim za"l:

clarification.explanation: One must make two bowings and two uprightenings in every bowing of the Amidah. How so: when saying "Baruch," one bows with the body alone, and at the word "Atah" he bows his head as well — these are the two bowings. And when he says the Name of God, he makes two uprightenings: first he straightens his body alone, and afterward his head as well — and there is a hint in this to the order of the journeys of the children of Israel in the wilderness, "as they encamped, so they journeyed" (that is, just as the order of encampment and travel were equal, so here the order of bowing and the order of straightening are equal to each other — body, then head). This is what our sages meant when they said, "Whoever bows, bows at 'Baruch,' and whoever straightens, straightens at the Name." The bowing should be until all the vertebrae of the spine protrude, and if he is elderly or ill and cannot bend that much, it suffices that he lower his head.
takeaways: Two bowings and two uprightenings in every bowing of the Amidah
At "Baruch" the body bows, at "Atah" the head bows, and at the Name he straightens body and then head — and there is a hint in this doubled order to "as they encamped, so they journeyed"
The bowing continues until the vertebrae of the spine protrude
An elderly or ill person may suffice with lowering his head

paragraphs: Ot va"v hannosepet betebat "velohe yaaqob", veot he" yetera shebbattebot "hael haggadol haggibbor vehannora", vegam ot va"v shel "vehannora", bekol echad veechad yesh sod gadol vekavvanot amuqqot, vetzarik hammitpallel lehotziam heteb bepiv shello yebulla echad mehem mechamat hammehirut, veal zeh neemar leadam heve zahir beot achat qalla ketiba achat chamura, sheen atta yodea hassod shel haotiyyot vehattebot hannizkarim battepilla, veim el sodam tidrosh, lek na reeh qetzat missodam beshaar hakkavvanot bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l vesiddur harasha"sh za"l:

clarification.explanation: The extra letter vav in the word "VeElohei Ya'akov," the extra letter heh in the words "HaEl HaGadol HaGibor VeHaNora," and also the vav of "VeHaNora" — in each of them there is a great secret and profound intentions. The one who prays must pronounce them well with his mouth, so that none of them is swallowed due to haste. And regarding this it was said that one should be as careful with a light letter as with a grave word, for you do not know the secret of the letters and words in the prayer. And whoever wishes to look into their secret may see a little of it in Sha'ar HaKavanot of the Ari and in the Siddur of the Rashash.
takeaways: The vav of "VeElohei Ya'akov," the heh of "HaEl," and the vav of "VeHaNora" contain a secret
One must pronounce them well with the mouth so that none is swallowed due to haste
Be as careful with a light letter as with a grave word, for you do not know their secret

paragraphs: Mah sheomerim "qoneh hakkol" lepi perush rashi"y bappasuq "qoneh shamayim vaaretz" (bereshit yd, yt) omero kan "qoneh hakkol" rotzeh lomar oseh hakkol, ulepi dibre hattargum veharamba"n sham beur "qoneh hakkol" rotzeh lomar qinyano hakkol dehakkol shello, ukemo shekkatabnu al pasuq "halo hu abik qaneka" (debarim lb, v):

clarification.explanation: Regarding the words in the blessing of Avot, "Koneh HaKol," according to Rashi's commentary on the verse "Koneh shamayim va'aretz" the meaning is "He makes all." And according to the Targum and the Ramban, the meaning of "Koneh HaKol" is that everything is His possession, that is, everything is His, as explained regarding the verse "Is not He your Father who acquired you?"
takeaways: "Koneh HaKol" according to Rashi means "He makes all"
According to the Targum and the Ramban it means that everything is His possession and belongs to Him

paragraphs: Mah sheomerim "gomel chasadim tobim" lepi peshuto muban shehu leshon gomel, ak mah shennireh misseper hakkavvanot detebat gomel hannizkar hu inyan hotzaa vegilluy keinyan "veyigmol sheqedim" (bammidbar yz, kg), perush motzi umamtzi umegaddel umetaqqen et haorot hanniqraim "chasadim tobim", umegalleh otam lehashpia, vachasadim tobim ellu hem sod mah sheamar hakkatub "chasde david hanneemanim" (yeshaya nh, g), veniqraim tobim lepi shehem mamshikim shepa el hayyesod tzaddiq olam hanniqra "tob", besod imru "tzaddiq ki tob" (yeshaya g, y) vekannizkar beseper hakkavvanot():

clarification.explanation: Regarding the words "Gomel chasadim tovim," according to their plain meaning they are an expression of bestowing kindness. But according to the secret, the word "gomel" here is a matter of bringing forth and revealing, like "vayigmol shekedim," meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, brings forth, produces, develops, and perfects the lights called "good kindnesses," and reveals them so as to bestow their influence. These good kindnesses are the secret of "the sure kindnesses of David," and are called "good" because they draw forth the flow to the sefirah called "Tov" (good).
takeaways: "Gomel chasadim tovim" according to its plain meaning is an expression of bestowing kindness
According to the secret, "gomel" is an expression of bringing forth and revealing the lights of kindness
The good kindnesses draw forth the flow to the sefirah called "Tov"

paragraphs: Mah sheomerim "vezoker chasde abot" lepi peshutan shel debarim hu sheyyizkor hachasadim shehibticha bahem et haabot lehetib lahem ulezaram, vedomeh lazeh yesh bappasuq "chasde david hanneemanim" (yeshaya nh, g), o hakkavvana kan al derek mah shepperesh hammetzudot bappasuq "zakera lechasde david abdeka" bedibre hayyamim b' siman v' (pasuq mb), veken kan sheyyizkor hachasadim sheasu haabot baolam ubizkutam yerachem alenu, veal derek hassod hu mah sheomerim "vezoker chasde abot" hakkavvana al shelosha orot chesed gebura tiperet nimshakim min shelosha rishonot hanniqraim abot, velaken chesed gebura tiperet niqraim "chasde abot" rotzeh lomar chasadim hannimshakim min shelosha rishonot hanniqraim abot, veyaan dekullam niklalim bechesed niqraim kullam beshem chasadim vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot bidrush b' dap l"b ammud b :

clarification.explanation: Regarding the words "VeZocher chasdei avot," according to the plain meaning the intent is that the Holy One, blessed be He, remembers the kindnesses He promised to the Patriarchs, to do good to them and to their descendants. Or the intent is that He remembers the kindnesses the Patriarchs performed in the world, and in their merit shows us mercy. And by way of secret, the intent is the three lights of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet that flow from the first three sefirot called Fathers, and therefore they are called "chasdei avot," and since they are all included within Chesed they are all called by the name "kindnesses."
takeaways: "VeZocher chasdei avot" according to the plain meaning: He remembers the kindnesses He promised to the Patriarchs
Or: He remembers the kindnesses the Patriarchs performed, and in their merit shows us mercy
According to the secret: the lights of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet that flow from the Patriarchs

paragraphs: Mah sheomerim "umebi goel libne benehem" hakkavvana bipshutan shel debarim dehashshebatim hemma benehem shel haabot, vekol yisrael hem bene hashshebatim, velaken yisrael niqraim bene benehem shel haabot, veomerim ken kede leorer zekut hashshebatim gam ken, velaken lo ameru "umebi goel libnehem", veal derek hassod shelosh harishonot hem abot lishlosha emtzaiyyot chesed gebura tiperet, ki chesed gebura tiperet nechshabim banim lishlosha rishonot, vehashshelosha acharonot netzach hod yesod niqraim bene benehem shel shelosha rishonot, vekannizkar beseper hakkavvanot():

clarification.explanation: Regarding the words "U'mevi go'el livnei veneihem," according to the plain meaning the tribes are the children of the Patriarchs, and all of Israel are the children of the tribes, and therefore Israel is called the children's children of the Patriarchs; this is said in order to arouse the merit of the tribes as well, and therefore they did not say simply "to their children." And by way of secret, the first three sefirot are fathers to the three middle ones, Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet, and the last three, Netzach, Hod, and Yesod, are the children's children of the first ones.
takeaways: "Their children's children": Israel are the children of the tribes, who are the children of the Patriarchs
This is said in order to arouse the merit of the tribes as well
According to the secret: the last sefirot are the children's children of the first ones

paragraphs: Kesheyyaggia lemillat "beahaba" yekavven limsor napsho al qiddush hashshem kannizkar bekavvanot rabbenu haari"y za"l(), velaken minhag hachasidim sheyyaarik hachazzan bachazara betebat "beahaba" kede leorer hakkavvana hannizkeret, vekol adam yizzaher bazeh bekol tepillot belachash limsor atzmo al qiddush hashshem betebat "beahaba", ukesheomer "umoshia umagen" yekavven betebat "magen" shehu mispar shelosh peamim "l:

clarification.explanation: When one reaches the word "be'ahavah" in the blessing of Avot, he should have in mind to give up his soul for the sanctification of God's Name, as explained in the intentions of the Ari. Therefore it is the custom of the Chassidim that the cantor prolongs "be'ahavah" in the repetition to arouse this intent. And every person should be careful in every silent prayer to devote himself to the sanctification of God's Name at the word "be'ahavah." And when he says "u'moshia u'magen," he should have in mind at the word "magen" that it has the numerical value of three times the Name "E-l."
takeaways: At the word "be'ahavah" in the blessing of Avot, one has in mind to give up his soul for the sanctification of God's Name
The cantor prolongs "be'ahavah" in the repetition to arouse this intent
In every silent prayer one should devote himself to the sanctification of God's Name at "be'ahavah"
At the word "magen," one has in mind that it equals three times the Name "E-l"

paragraphs: Bibraka shel "atta gibbor" yekavven berashe tebot "atta gibbor leolam adonay" hashshem gl", vekatab harab bet david za"l mah sheomerim "leolam" rotzeh lomar lo kebasar vadam shello yishshaer bigburato beet ziqnato shemmishtanneh, abal "atta gibbor leolam" ki en ziqna lepaneka velo yihyeh beka shinnuy ayyen sham, umah sheomerim bibraka zo inyan geshem vetal, mippene shebbiridat geshem vetal yihyeh berur nitzotzot qedushsha min domem letzomeach, vehabberur shel nitzotzot qedushsha hu kemo techiyyat hammetim, delaken ameru rabbotenu zikronam libraka gadol yom haggeshamim keyom techiyyat hammetim, veken ameru yom haggeshamim yeshua para veraba bo, velaken omerim "somek nopelim" keneged berur nitzotzot qedushsha shennapelu bechay medabber beshibim ummot, "verope cholim" keneged nitzotzot qedushsha shehem bechay bilti medabber, "umattir asurim" keneged nitzotzot qedushsha shebbatztzomeach, "umeqayyem emunato lishene apar" keneged hannitzotzot qedushsha shebbedomem, ulekak lo hizkiru kan ella raq arbaa leshonot shel shebach ellu shehem keneged domem tzomeach chay medabber meilla letatta, velo ameru shear shebachim shel "poqeach ivrim" u"zoqep kepupim" vekayyotze ukemo shekkatabti kol zeh besipri haq' "mqbtzyl", ubeamero "mekalkel chayyim bechesed" yekavven leshem hvy"h bemilluy yodin sheoleh mispar "chesed":

clarification.explanation: In the blessing "Atah Gibor" one should have in mind, in the acronym "Atah Gibor Le'olam Adonai," the Name Agla. And Rav Beit David wrote that "le'olam" means: not like flesh and blood, whose might changes in old age, but "You are mighty forever," since there is no old age or change before You. And they mention in this blessing the matter of rain and dew, because through their descent the sparks of holiness are clarified from the mineral to the vegetative, and this clarification is similar to the resurrection of the dead, and therefore our sages said, "The day of rains is as great as the day of the resurrection of the dead." And therefore we say "Somech noflim," "Verofe cholim," "U'matir asurim," "U'mekayem emunato lishenei afar," corresponding to the four clarifications of mineral, vegetative, animate, and speaking. And in saying "Mechalkel chaim b'chesed," he should have in mind the Name Havayah spelled out with the letter yud, which has the numerical value of "chesed."
takeaways: In the blessing "Atah Gibor" one has in mind the acronym forming the Name Agla
"Le'olam" means that there is no old age or change before God
Rain and dew are mentioned because their descent brings about a clarification of sparks of holiness resembling the resurrection of the dead
Four praises correspond to mineral, vegetative, animate, and speaking, and "Mechalkel chaim" equals "chesed" in gematria

paragraphs: Beur birkat "atta qadosh" hu kemo shekkatab rabbenu mahara"m alshek za"l kelomar atta lebaddeka qadosh, veshimka hamyuchad hu haqqadosh deap al pi shenneemar toar qadosh lammalakim eno atzmi ella bederek hashsheela, yaan ki "uqedoshim" hem hammalakim shenniqraim qedoshim, hemma "yehalluka sela" bashshebach hazzeh shel "qadosh qadosh qadosh", veim etzlam qadosh toar atzmi, ek yehalluka betoar shennimtza ittam:

clarification.explanation: The explanation of the blessing "Atah Kadosh" is as Maharam Alshech wrote: You alone are holy, and Your unique Name is the Holy One. And even though the title "holy" is also said of the angels, this is not an essential title for them but only borrowed, since the angels, who are called "holy ones," are the ones who "praise You, Selah" with the praise "Holy, Holy, Holy" — and were holiness an essential title of theirs, how could they praise You with a title that belongs to themselves?
takeaways: "Atah Kadosh": You alone are holy, and Your Name is the Holy One
The title "holy" as applied to the angels is not essential but borrowed
The angels praise with "Holy, Holy, Holy" — it cannot be that they praise with a title that is their own

paragraphs: Bimot hachamma im nistappeq shemma hizkir geshem, haddin hu ad sheloshim yom im hu mistappeq amerinan chazaqa shehizkir geshem, vetzarik lachazor, veachar sheloshim yom en tzarik lachazor, veim nizdammen deachar sheloshim yom taa ubarur lo shettaa paam o paamayim vechazar hattepilla, veachar kak nizdammen bepaam acheret shennistappeq katabti besipri haq' "mqbtzyl" kevan dikbar huchzaq sheloshim yom shello taa bahem, ap al gab deachar sheloshim yom taa lo ibbed hachazaqa, vekol heka denistappeq amerinan shehizkir kahogen kaasher hurgal beotam hashsheloshim yom, mihu im lo huchzaq sheloshim yom shehizkir kahogen, ella barur lo shettaa betok hashsheloshim yom en lazeh chezqat sheloshim, vekol shehu mistappeq hare zeh chozer veim hitpallel sheloshim velo nizdammen lo bahem shettaa beberur ella nizdammen shennistappeq ulekak chazar bishbil hassapeq, pasaqti deim achar hashsheloshim chazar venistappeq hare zeh chozer lehitpallel veyatneh bedato qodem deim lo taa tihyeh tepillato betorat nedaba, veim taa tihyeh betorat choba, veayyen bet david siman mz shehebiu "machaziq beraka" siman qyz, veayyen "iqqere hd"t" v"chesed laalapim" v"ohel yitzchaq chasid" siman :

clarification.explanation: In the summer months, if one is in doubt whether he mistakenly mentioned "Morid hagashem": within thirty days from the start of summer, if he is in doubt, we say there is a presumption that he mentioned rain as he was accustomed, and he must repeat the prayer. After thirty days he need not repeat, since he has already grown accustomed to the correct text. And if after thirty days he happens to err clearly once or twice and repeats, and afterward becomes doubtful again, he does not lose the presumption of the thirty days, and whenever he is in doubt we say that he mentioned it properly. But if he had not established a presumption of thirty days of mentioning it properly, and rather it is clear to him that he erred within them, he has no such presumption, and whenever in doubt he must repeat. And one who prayed thirty days without clearly erring, but only became doubtful and repeated on account of the doubt — if after the thirty days he becomes doubtful again, he repeats and prays, stipulating in his mind that if he did not err his prayer shall be a voluntary offering, and if he did err it shall be an obligatory prayer.
takeaways: In doubt whether he mentioned rain in the summer: within thirty days he repeats due to the presumption
After thirty days he does not repeat, since he has grown accustomed to the correct text
Erring clearly after thirty days does not cause the loss of the presumption
One who prayed thirty days only in doubt, if in doubt again, repeats and stipulates that it be a voluntary offering

paragraphs: Bimot haggeshamim sheshshakach lomar "morid haggeshem" veamar "morid hattal" eno chozer yaan deamar morid hattal, veim kol zeh im nizkar qodem shehitchil "atta qadosh" yomar "sham mashshib harucha umorid haggeshem", deap al pi shessiyyem habberaka shel "mechayyeh hammetim", kevan dela hitchil babberaka sheachareha lo niqra siyyum beraka leinyan zeh: veda dishlosha berakot rishonot chashubot keachat, veken shelosha acharonot name chashubot keachat, lepikak bekol maqom shettaa bishlosha rishonot chozer lerosh hattepilla, ubishlosha acharonot chozer laaboda:

clarification.explanation: In the rainy season, one who forgot to say "Morid hagashem" and said "Morid hatal" instead does not repeat the prayer, since he did say "Morid hatal." Nevertheless, if he remembers before beginning the blessing "Atah Kadosh," he should say there instead "Mashiv haruach u'morid hagashem," for even though he has finished the blessing "Mechayeh hameitim," since he has not yet begun the following blessing, this is not considered the conclusion of a blessing for this purpose. And know that the first three blessings are considered as one, and likewise the last three are considered as one. Therefore, wherever one errs in the first three, he returns to the beginning of the prayer, and in the last three he returns to "Retzeh" ("Avodah").
takeaways: Forgetting "Morid hagashem" and saying "Morid hatal" instead — he does not repeat
If he remembers before "Atah Kadosh," he says "Mashiv haruach u'morid hagashem" there instead
The first three blessings are considered as one, and the last three are considered as one
Erring in the first three, he returns to the beginning; erring in the last three, he returns to "Retzeh"

paragraphs: Beur birkat "hashibenu" katabti besipri haq' "mqbtzyl" al pi mah shekkatab rabbenu haari"y za"l shehaadam al yede aonotayv gorem lesalleq or haqqedushsha hannimshak alenu min hattora umin hattepilla vehammitzot, ayyen besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l bebeur "vayhi noam veku'", velazeh mitpallelin "hashibenu abinu letorateka" hu or haqqedushsha hannimshak alenu al yede eseq hattora, "uqerabenu malkenu laabodateka" hu or haqqedushsha shennimshak alenu mittepilla umitzot dehem niqraim aboda, "vehachazirenu bitshuba shelema lepaneka" hi teshuba illaa hammaggaat ad kisse hakkabod, ad vead biklal sheyyehe babbina shehu sod kisse, gam omeram "teshuba shelema" lomar shettezakkenu lachazor bitshuba al arba mine chattaot haamurim bearba chilluqe kappara bepereq batera deyoma bemaamar rabbi matya ben charash, shehem pogemim bearba otiyyot shem havaya"h baruk hu kamporash sodam bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar haggilgulim yeuyyan sham. vechotemim "harotzeh bitshuba" shehu rotzeh bekak qodem shehachote yitorer lashub, vegam rotzeh lomar shehu gazar bekak lepi middat harachamim, mah sheen ken hachakema vehannebua lo ratzu bekak ella bedin (yerushalmi makkot b, v):

clarification.explanation: The explanation of the blessing "Hashivenu" (as Rabbi Yosef Chaim wrote in his book "Makabtziel," based on the words of the Ari): a person, through his sins, causes the removal of the light of holiness that flows to us from the Torah, from prayer, and from the mitzvot. Therefore we pray "Hashivenu avinu leToratecha" — this is the light of holiness that flows through engaging in Torah; "Vekarvenu malkeinu la'avodatecha" — the light of holiness that flows from prayer and the mitzvot, which are called "avodah"; "Vehachazirenu bitshuvah shelemah lefanecha" — this is the supreme repentance that reaches all the way to the Throne of Glory, and including it, that it be in the aspect of "Binah," which is the secret of "the Throne." And also saying "teshuvah shelemah" — that we merit to repent for the four kinds of sins mentioned in the four categories of atonement (at the end of tractate Yoma, in the statement of Rabbi Matya ben Charash), which blemish the four letters of the Name Havayah, as explained in the secret of the matter in the writings of the Ari in Sha'ar HaGilgulim. And they conclude with "HaRotzeh bitshuvah" — meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, desires repentance even before the sinner is aroused to repent, and also meaning that He decreed this by the attribute of mercy; which is not so with the attributes of Wisdom and Prophecy, which did not desire this except by strict justice alone (as brought in the Yerushalmi, tractate Makkot).
takeaways: The blessing "Hashivenu" expresses three levels: the restoration of the light of holiness from Torah, from prayer, and from the mitzvot, and supreme repentance reaching the Throne of Glory (in the aspect of Binah)
"Teshuvah shelemah" also refers to the rectification of four kinds of sins that blemish the four letters of the Name Havayah
The conclusion "HaRotzeh bitshuvah" teaches that the attribute of mercy desires the sinner's repentance at once, unlike the attributes of Wisdom and Prophecy, which require strict justice first

paragraphs: Im bimot hachamma amar "barek alenu" tzarik lachazor lomar "barekenu", ak kede shello yihyeh nireh kenussach beraka achat shehizkir bah matar venimtza shello tiqqen kelum, laken yishtoq kede hilluk arba ammot o yoter veachar kak yatchil lomar "berukkenu" vekannizkar b"chesed laalapim" siman qyb ot y: veim bimot haggeshamim amar "barekenu" velo shaal matar, im nizkar achar shessiyyem habberaka qodem shehitchil "taqa bashshopar" omer sham "veten tal umatar libraka" vedayyo, veim nizkar achar shehitchil b"taqa" en tzarik lachazor, ella yomar b"shomea tepilla" "veten tal umatar libraka ki atta shomea tepillat kol peh veku'", veim haya lo taanit beoto hayyom yomar sheelat tal umatar b"shomea tepilla" qodem sheyyomar "anenu", veim lo nizkar ella ad achar shessiyyem "shomea tepilla", qodem shehitchil "retzeh" yomar sham "veten tal umatar libraka", veim nizkar achar shehitchil "retzeh" az chozer lebirkat hashshanim veomer al hasseder, veim lo nizkar ella ad leachar sheamar "yihyu leratzon imre pi" haacharon hassamuk l"oseh shalom", az apillu sheadayin lo aqar raglayv tzarik lachazor lehatchalat tepillat haamida:

clarification.explanation: In the summer months, if one said by mistake "Barech aleinu" (the winter formula), he must go back and say "Barchenu." But so that it should not appear as though he said one continuous formula in which he both mentioned rain and corrected it, he should first pause for the duration of walking four amot, and only then begin "Barchenu." And in the rainy season, if one said "Barchenu" and did not request rain: if he remembers after finishing the blessing but before beginning "Teka bashofar," he says there, "Veten tal u'matar livrachah," and that suffices. If he remembers after having begun "Teka," he need not repeat, but says in "Shome'a tefillah," "Veten tal u'matar livrachah." If he was fasting that day, he says the request for dew and rain in "Shome'a tefillah" before "Aneinu." If he remembers only after finishing "Shome'a tefillah," before "Retzeh," he says it there. If he remembers after having begun "Retzeh," he returns to Birkat HaShanim and continues in order. If he does not remember until after the final "Yihyu leratzon," he must return to the beginning of the Amidah, even if he has not yet stepped from his place.
takeaways: In summer, one who said "Barech aleinu" pauses for the time of walking four amot and then says "Barchenu"
One who forgot rain and remembers before "Teka" says it there instead; after "Teka," he says it in "Shome'a tefillah"
Remembering before "Retzeh," he says it at the end of "Shome'a tefillah"; after "Retzeh," he returns to Birkat HaShanim
Not remembering until after the final "Yihyu leratzon," he returns to the beginning of the Amidah

paragraphs: Eretz achat kullah shetztzerikim lematar bimot hachamma en shoalin oto betzibbur apillu b"shomea tepilla" ella yomru "barekenu" kerub haolam, abal kol yachid veyachid rashshay lishol matar b"shomea tepilla" beotah haaretz hatztzerika lematar bimot hachamma, dehaynu sheomer b"shomea tepilla" "veten tal umatar libraka" bitpillat lachash davqa, abal lomar "barek alenu" apillu hayyachid belachash eno rashshay, veken shelicha tzibbur bachazara eno rashshay lishol matar apillu b"shomea tepilla", veim hayyachid taa veamar "barek alenu" yesayyem tepillato, veyachazor veyitpallel achar kak betorat nedaba veyomar bah "barekenu" veayyen "shalme tzibbur" dap qal:

clarification.explanation: In a land that entirely needs rain in the summer months, the congregation does not request rain, even in "Shome'a tefillah," but says "Barchenu" like the rest of the world. But each individual is permitted to request rain in "Shome'a tefillah," specifically in the silent prayer, in that land which needs rain, saying "Veten tal u'matar livrachah." But to say "Barech aleinu" is not permitted even for an individual in silent prayer, nor for the prayer leader in the repetition, even in "Shome'a tefillah." And if the individual erred and said "Barech aleinu," he should finish his prayer and afterward pray again as a voluntary offering, saying in it "Barchenu."
takeaways: In a land that needs rain in summer, the congregation says "Barchenu" and does not request rain even in "Shome'a tefillah"
The individual is permitted to request rain in "Shome'a tefillah," specifically in the silent prayer
One does not say "Barech aleinu" even individually in silent prayer, nor does the prayer leader in the repetition
One who erred and said "Barech aleinu" finishes his prayer and prays again as a voluntary offering, saying "Barchenu"

paragraphs: Kesheomer "vekol oyebeka vekol soneeka" yekavven "oyebeka" al s"m "vesoneeka" al lilit, veken yekavven gam ken bazot bebirkat "hashiba" kesheomer "vehaser mimmennu yagon" al s"m "vaanacha" al lilit vekannizkar besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, veyizzaher bibraka shel hamminim shello yomar ella raq arbaa leshonot ellu "teaqer tishshaber tikkalem vetakniem" vaalehem en lehosip umehem en ligroa ki hem keneged qelippat nogah deaatzilut beria yetzira asiyya kemo shekkatebu hamqubbalim za"l veayyen "minchat aharon" kelal tz ot kt ukesheomer bibraka d"l hatztzaddiqim" "vesim chelqenu immahem", yekavven lehitpallel lehashshem yitbarek sheim garemu aonotayv sheyyittol cheleq olam habba shello chas veshalom veyinnaten latztzaddiqim acherim, sheyyinnaten beyad tzaddiq sheeno chapetz lehanot mishshel acherim kede sheyyachazirehu lo kesheyyashub bitshuba ukemo shekkatub beseper hakkavvanot, ukesheomer bebirkat "tishkon veku'" "vekisse david abdeka mehera betokah takin", yekavven lehitpallel bazeh al mashicha ben yosep shello yehareg al yede armilos harasha, deal mashicha ben yosep anachnu omerim "kisse david abdeka veku'" vekannizkar beseper hakkavvanot, ubeseper peri etz chayyim" katub sheyyekavven gam ken al shelemot hakkisse beot ' sheyyihyeh hakkisse shalem veyair hakketer sham. veomero "binyan olam" sheyyihyeh qayyam leolam, velo kebinyan harishon shehaya al yede adam venechrab, ubeamero "ki lishuateka qivvinu" yekavven letzappot lishua beemet:

clarification.explanation: In the blessing "VeLamalshinim," when one says "Vechol oyvecha vechol son'echa," he should have in mind "oyvecha" as referring to the evil power called Samael, and "son'echa" as referring to Lilith; and likewise in the blessing "Hashivah shofteinu," when saying "Vehaser mimenu yagon," he should have in mind Samael, and "anachah" as Lilith. And he should be careful in the blessing concerning heretics to say only these four expressions, "Te'aker tishaver tikalem vetachnium," and nothing should be added or subtracted, for they correspond to the kelipah of Nogah in the four worlds Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah. And when he says in the blessing of the righteous, "Vesim chelkeinu imahem," he should have in mind to pray that if his sins caused his portion in the World to Come to be taken, it be given into the hand of a righteous person who does not wish to benefit from what belongs to others, so that he return it to him when he returns in repentance. And when he says "Vechisei David avdecha meherah betochah tachin," he should have in mind to pray for Mashiach ben Yosef, that he not be killed by Armilus the wicked. And in the book "Pri Etz Chaim" it is written that one should also have in mind the completeness of the throne, that at the letter alef (of "Kisei David avdecha") the throne be complete and the Keter shine within it. And in saying "Binyan olam," he should have in mind that the Temple will endure forever, and not like the first building, which was built by human hands and was destroyed. And in saying "Ki lishuatcha kivinu," he should have in mind to truly await the salvation.
takeaways: In "VeLamalshinim" one has in mind "oyvecha" as Samael and "son'echa" as Lilith, and likewise in "Hashivah"
In the blessing concerning heretics, only these four expressions: "te'aker tishaver tikalem vetachnium," corresponding to the four worlds
"Vesim chelkeinu imahem": that if one's portion is taken, it be given to a righteous person who will return it to him when he repents
"Vechisei David": one has in mind Mashiach ben Yosef, that he not be killed by Armilus

One should also have in mind: the completeness of the throne and the light of the Keter at the letter alef (Sefer Pri Etz Chaim), the everlasting endurance of the Temple at "Binyan olam," and a true hope for salvation at "Ki lishuatcha kivinu"

paragraphs: Bebirkat "modim" yikra b"modim" veyizqop beshem, vegam kan yaaseh shette keriot ushette zeqipot kemo shekkatabti leel bebirkat abot, veap al pi shebbeseper hakkavvanot() meporash deday beachat ki hashsheniyya mashlim b"modim derabbanan", hinneh kebar ba chakam hu rabbenu harasha"sh za"l vediqdeq middibre rabbenu haari"y za"l bemaqom acher sheggam kan tzarik shette keriot ushette zeqipot, veap al gab deharab "shemen zayit zak" dap ql"ch katab deen laasot hepek hamporash beseper hakkavvanot ayyen sham, hinneh meachar sheddibre rabbenu harasha"sh za"l hem mukrachim, umilleshon seper hakkavvanot lo mashma deyesh ikkub baddabar lebilti asot shette keriot ushette zeqipot ella katab deeno tzarik, al ken vadday yesh laasot kedibre harasha"sh za"l shette keriot ushette zeqipot:

clarification.explanation: In the blessing "Modim," one bows at "Modim" and straightens at the Name, and here too one does two bowings and two uprightenings, as in the blessing of Avot. And although Sefer HaKavanot explicitly states that one bowing suffices, since the second is completed at "Modim DeRabbanan," the Rashash already derived precisely from the words of the Ari elsewhere that here too two bowings and two uprightenings are required. And although the "Shemen Zayit Zach" wrote that one should not act opposite to what is explicit in Sefer HaKavanot, nevertheless, since the words of the Rashash are compelling, and since the language of Sefer HaKavanot does not indicate an actual prohibition against doing two, but only that it is not required, one should certainly follow the Rashash and do two bowings and two uprightenings.
takeaways: In the blessing "Modim" one bows at "Modim" and straightens at the Name
One does two bowings and two uprightenings, as in the blessing of Avot
The Rashash derived that two are required here as well, and although some disagree, this is the primary ruling

paragraphs: Im yesh lo roq al yashoach b"modim" ella yabliennu biksuto veachar kak yashoach b"modim", umah sheomerim "ereb uboqer vetzahorayim" qae al "nodeh leka unesapper tehillateka", ukeillu amar kak "ereb uboqer vetzahorayim nodeh lak unesapper tehillatak al chayyenu hammesurim beyadeka veku'", ubebirkat "sim shalom" yomar "uberukkenu abinu kullanu keechad beor paneka", veachar siyyum beraka zo yomar miyyad "yihyu leratzon imre pi", veqodem sheomer pasuq zeh en lehapsiq apillu leqaddish uqedushsha vekayyotze, ki pasuq zeh hu mikkelal tepillat haamida, abal achar pasuq "yihyu leratzon" yapsiq lekol debar qedushsha vaapillu leummanim dibrakot:

clarification.explanation: If one has saliva in his mouth, he should not bow immediately at "Modim," but rather swallow it discreetly into his garment and only then bow. And the words "Erev vavoker vetzohorayim" refer to "Nodeh lecha unsaper tehilatecha," as though one said: "Evening, morning, and noon we thank You and recount Your praise for our lives entrusted into Your hand, etc." And in the blessing "Sim shalom," one says "Uvarchenu avinu kulanu ke'echad be'or panecha," and immediately after concluding this blessing he says "Yihyu leratzon imrei fi." Before saying this verse one does not interrupt even for Kaddish or Kedushah, since this verse is part of the Amidah prayer; but after "Yihyu leratzon" one may interrupt for any matter of sanctity, and even to answer amen to blessings.
takeaways: One who has saliva swallows it discreetly into his garment and then bows at "Modim"
"Erev vavoker vetzohorayim" refers to "Nodeh lecha unsaper tehilatecha"
After "Sim shalom" one says "Yihyu leratzon" immediately, since it is part of the Amidah
Before "Yihyu leratzon" one does not interrupt for Kaddish or Kedushah, but afterward one may interrupt for any matter of sanctity

paragraphs: Qodem "elohay netzor" yesh nohagim lomar mizmor "shir lammaalot essa enay el heharim", umatu bah mishshem harab mosheh zekuta za"l ubedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l lo nizkar zeh, ak beseper hakkavvanot dap q' ammud g katub lomar mizmor "elohim yechannenu" betzurat hammenora qodem "elohay netzor" ayyen sham, vekol echad yaaseh kepi minhago bazeh, ukesheyyomar "lemaan yechaletzun yedideka" yekavven rashe tebot shem qadosh yl"y vehu hammaaleh nitzotzot, veachar shettomar "hoshia yemineka vaaneni" yomar tekep "yihyu leratzon imre pi" paam shenit, veyesh nohagim lomar tepillat rab shehi y" peamim "chayyim" uminhag yapeh hu, ubi"chesed laalapim" katab: achar sheyyomar "umalak Adonai docheh", yomar "qabbel rinnat ammeka sheggibbeno tiharnu nora", vikavven berashe tebot beshem "qera sht"n", veachar kol hattachanunim shennoheg lehosip yachzor lomar paam shelishit "yihyu leratzon":

clarification.explanation: Before "Elohai netzor," some have the custom of saying the psalm "Essa einai" (I lift my eyes) in the name of Rav Moshe Zacuto, and this is not mentioned in the words of the Ari; but Sefer HaKavanot writes to say the psalm "Elohim yechonenu" arranged in the shape of the Menorah before "Elohai netzor," and each person follows his own custom. And when he says "Lema'an yechaletzun yedidecha," he should have in mind the acronym of the holy Name Yali, which raises up sparks. And after "Hoshi'ah yeminecha va'aneni," he says "Yihyu leratzon" a second time immediately. Some have the custom of saying the Prayer of Rav, eleven mentions of "chayim," and this is a fine custom. And in "Chesed LaAlafim" it is written that after "Umalach Hashem docheh" one says "Kabel rinat amcha, sagvenu, taharenu, nora," with the intent of the acronym "Kera Satan." And after all the supplications one adds, he returns to say "Yihyu leratzon" a third time.
takeaways: Some say the psalm "Essa einai" before "Elohai netzor," and some say "Elohim yechonenu" arranged in the shape of the Menorah
At "Lema'an yechaletzun yedidecha" one has in mind the acronym of the Name Yali
After "Hoshi'ah yeminecha va'aneni" one says "Yihyu leratzon" a second time
Some say the Prayer of Rav, with the intent "Kera Satan," concluding with "Yihyu leratzon" a third time

paragraphs: Achar "yihyu leratzon" haacharon yipsa shelosha pesiot laachorayv, velo yarchiq raglo yoter mishshiur aqeb betzad gudal mammash, deyesh sod baddabar deellu hem keneged shelosha olamot beria yetzira asiyya, dehaadam baamida chosheb keillu omed baatzilut, veim hammaqom tzar yeqatztzer happesiot, ak lekattechilla lo yitpallel bemaqom tzar sheeno yakol laasot bo shelosha pesiot shekkol pesia hi aqeb betzad gudal, veyikra meat qodem happesiot, ubeodo korea achar hashshalosh pesiot yipneh lismolo veyomar "oseh shalom bimromayv", veyizqop, veyipneh limino veyikra qetzat veyomar "hu yaaseh shalom alenu", veyizqop, veyikra lepanayv veyomar "veal kol yisrael" veyizqop vekannizkar besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, ukesheoqer raglayv oqer regel semol techilla, ubemaqom shekkalu pesiotayv yishheh sham ad sheyyaggia shelicha tzibbur laqqedushsha, veaz yachzor shelosh pesiot lepanayv veyaggia limqomo harishon shehitpallel bo velo yachazir panayv latztzibbur, vetob lehaqpid shello yelek adam lepanayv bemaqom shekkalu pesiotayv, veim heerik bitpillato vesiyyem achar sheameru qedushsha, veken im mitpallel beyachid lo yachzor limqom amidato tekep achar sheppasa, ella yamtin mahalak arba ammot laamod bemaqom shekkalu pesiotayv umaskil al kol dabar yimtza tob:

clarification.explanation: After the final "Yihyu leratzon," one steps three steps backward, each step being heel beside toe, corresponding to the three worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, since during the Amidah a person considers himself as standing in Atzilut. If the place is narrow he shortens the steps, but ideally one should not pray in a place too narrow for three such steps. He bows slightly before the steps, and while bowing, after the three steps, turns to his left and says "Oseh shalom bimromav" and straightens; turns to his right, bows, and says "Hu ya'aseh shalom aleinu" and straightens; bows forward and says "Ve'al kol Yisrael" and straightens. And when he lifts his feet to step, he lifts the left foot first. In the place where his steps end he remains until the prayer leader reaches the Kedushah, and then returns three steps forward to his original place, without turning his face to the congregation. And one who prayed alone, or finished after the Kedushah, should not return to his place immediately, but should wait the duration of walking four amot.
takeaways: After the final "Yihyu leratzon" one steps three steps backward, each step heel beside toe, corresponding to Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah
He bows and turns left at "Oseh shalom," right at "Hu ya'aseh," and forward at "Ve'al kol Yisrael"
He lifts the left foot first, and waits until the prayer leader reaches the Kedushah
